title: The Power of Outcome Focusing
coreMove: Declare what 'done' looks like in one concrete sentence before choosing any next action, so every commitment has a visible close condition the system can actually track.

exampleSpecs.domain: a charge nurse trying to clear a discharge backlog before shift handover
exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse at a mid-size regional hospital managing six rooms
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a medically cleared patient waits another full shift because 'handle Room 14 discharge' stayed vague on the whiteboard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she catches herself writing 'handle Room 14 discharge' and rewrites it as 'patient has signed paperwork, transport is confirmed, and bed is flagged available' — the outcome declared, the next phone call obvious

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance translator reorganizing her open project list on a Sunday afternoon
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-employed translator working across three languages and four simultaneous clients
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether two overdue deliverables stay invisible on the list until a client follows up and the working relationship frays
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her list moves from category labels like 'Müller contract' to declared outcomes like 'Müller legal brief returned with tracked changes accepted and final invoice sent' — the vagueness that masked the real work becomes visible and the gap between where she is and where she needs to be is suddenly measurable

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school drama teacher presenting a budget request in a department meeting
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-school drama teacher with a $2,400 production budget and six weeks until opening night
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the budget request is approved or bounced back because neither the teacher nor the department head could picture what a successful production actually requires
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher says 'we need to pull this show together' and the department head asks 'what does pulled together look like on opening night, specifically' — the question exposes that the outcome has never been declared, and the approval stalls not from budget politics but from a missing sentence

exampleSpecs.domain: a fourth-year PhD student staring at a two-week-old 'revise dissertation' item on a Sunday morning
exampleSpecs.audience: a sociology doctoral candidate whose committee has requested methods-section revisions before a November defense
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the revisions keep stalling while the committee waits and the defense date slips into next semester
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes 'methods section revised with all committee notes addressed and version sent to advisor by Thursday' — the low-grade nagging quiets the moment the outcome exists somewhere outside his head, and the first action surfaces on its own: open the committee email from six weeks ago

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional operations manager reconstructing why a full-day territory planning offsite produced nothing actionable
exampleSpecs.audience: a regional manager overseeing fourteen branch locations who just ran a failed all-hands
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wasted day, a frustrated team, and a Q3 plan that still does not exist two weeks before it was due
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the review surfaces a single root cause: nobody had declared what a successful offsite looked like before the room filled — without an outcome, the group could not notice when they drifted, could not course-correct, and could not close

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook asked to develop a new small-plates section for a seasonal menu change
exampleSpecs.audience: a line cook at a mid-range restaurant who has cooked from other people's menus for three years but has never led development
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the chef's deadline is met or the cook hands in a vague draft of half-ideas that the chef has to rebuild from scratch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she imagines the printed menu with the section already complete — five dishes listed, portion notes included — and the image makes the first action obvious before any planning happens: write down five candidate dishes tonight before tomorrow's prep shift starts
